note: Harbour light (Glint, 007 D). One low warm sun, one haze colour, a sky graded from pale warm horizon to soft blue, then grade and bloom. Read by Look after look.json and wins for the keys it holds (sun, ambient, fog, sky, skyGradient, post, reflection); the palette keys here are lighting colours only. Haze = light.haze: the fog colour, the sky horizon, the below-horizon colour and the reflection horizon are all it, so far geometry, sea edge and the horizon band dissolve into one colour. Concept bar: concepts/AtomicAge, Blocks and Streets/spaceage contact sheets (round 2: clear air in the city, haze only at the horizon, cream bright not beige, crisp shadows). No colour constants in C#.

sun.exposureMatch: Glint, brief 075-A: the whole old light rig is ported at our sun's level. The old reel ran sun 3 under post exposure -0.8; every light value of it is here multiplied by 0.6 (= 1.8 / 3) in linear and the exposure raised by log2(3 / 1.8) = +0.737 EV to -0.063. For everything the sun, ambient and sky light (the stone, the sea, the sky, the fog) the displayed frame is the same as the old reel's, while the things the game calibrated at our exposure (the crossing heads, the silhouette ink and rim that must stay under the bloom, the day emissives, the night look) keep their values. Scaled: sun 3 -> 1.8, ambient (value 0.79 on the old colours, about 0.6 in linear), the sky's stored colours (spaceSky, each channel solved through Unity's sRGB step so the shader sees exactly 0.6 x the old), the long haze, the bloom threshold 0.8 -> 0.48.

The old reel's sun (DecoKitStreet, old-keys.json light dump): intensity 3 (here 1.8, see exposureMatch), colour (1, 0.93, 0.8) = #ffedcc, 44.7 degrees up. The yaw stays 330: the old azimuth (-135 from the old boulevard's +z) belongs to the old street's frame; 330 keeps the civic square and the cafe terrace lit in the home frame (008 B5).

Honest frames showed B5's orange came from the grade, not the sun: the highlights tint (1, 0.85, 0.66) is a full-strength multiplier above luma 0.55 and the colour filter warmed everything. Both are neutral now, the sun keeps the warmth (colour unchanged, #ffe0d0), and the intensity rises 1.35 -> 1.6 to pay back what the tint took (1.7 puts 11 percent of the home frame at R 246 or more, 1.6 puts 4 percent), with the ambient down 10 percent so shade stays shade. Sun paving (238, 206, 169) -> about (237, 217, 198), the paintings' lit paving (mean of four: 240, 220, 201). Evidence: briefs/008/light-honest/.

shadows.note: Latch, brief 007 round 3 (Glint to tune). The sun's shadows for the orthographic tactical camera (views.json export views; the game's play camera). The camera stands back only as far as the geometry in its frame column needs (about 85 m at the civic square, 420 m under SpaceHQ); TacticalShadows sets the URP shadow distance to that depth + farBand (fading out over the last `fade` m: URP fades by distance from the camera, so a share-of-distance border faded the street itself at 400 m) and puts the last cascade on the street band [depth - nearBand, depth + farBand] while the camera renders, then restores the asset. At zoom 14 the band's cascade is ~5 cm per shadow texel (4096 atlas, 2048 per cascade): about 2 px at 1080p. Soft shadows (URP high-quality PCF) stay on. Other cameras keep the URP asset's own distance (views.json / flyby.json shadowDistance). Latch, 008 B6: cascades 4 -> 2 (one air cascade and the street band; Redline fix 3), so a tall block no longer redraws into three air cascades; airSplits stay for 3-4 cascades (the perf harness as-was switch).

spaceSky.note: Glint, brief 075-A (2026-10-28). The old reel's day sky, not a lookalike: DecoKit/Space Age Sky (Shaders/DecoKit/DK_SpaceSky.shader, the old DK_SpaceSky.shader ported verbatim plus inert evening hooks) with the old DK_Sky_Street.mat's values (~/Projects/the-suborned/game/Assets/TheSuborned/Art/DecoKit/Generated/DK_Sky_Street.mat, sha256 40ca9140...; the colours at 0.6 in linear for our sun, see coloursOld and sun.exposureMatch; every other value as stored), set by Atmosphere.SpaceSky with SetColor / SetVector as DecoKitSky.Apply set them, so Unity's sRGB-to-linear step on material colours applies as it did there (that is why the stored colours are above 1: DecoKitSky.Apply multiplied its sampled colours by the sky gain 1.5 = the a channel). It replaces skyGradient by day; night keeps night.skyGradient. Teal zenith and mid (the old 88,168,170 and 127,218,208), the warm horizon haze (246,229,195), the sun disc and aureole (glare: the haze brightens toward the sun), wind-stretched cirrus from the old noise sheet, and the old far-city band (DK_Skyline_Far, -1 to 9 degrees, gain 1.1) tinted by the haze of its own azimuth. The planet and moons are drawn by our horizon band as geometry (brief 007 E, 072), so their radii here are 0 (RaySphere never hits; the ring needs the planet's radius, so it goes with it). _SunDir is our sun's, set by the builder. Textures are the old files, byte for byte, in Resources/Atmosphere (new GUIDs, the old import settings).
spaceSky.coloursOld: the old .mat's stored values: _Zenith (0.14638105, 0.58735883, 0.6029668), _Mid (0.31834608, 1.051653, 0.9461358), _Horizon (1.3823731, 1.1753069, 0.8185868), _SunColor (1.5, 1.356992, 1.0956913), _CirrusColor (1.425, 1.425, 1.4399999), a 1.5 / 0.6; `colours` are these solved per channel so that after Unity's sRGB-to-linear step the shader sees 0.6 x the old linear value (light.json sun.exposureMatch).

ocean.note: Glint, brief 075-A (2026-10-28; water ownership agreed in briefs/075/notes.md: the shader and its light response are Glint's). The old reel's sea: Suborned/DK Ocean (Shaders/DecoKit/DK_Ocean.shader, the old DecoKit/Ocean ported verbatim plus our far-shore fade, the perspective haze, instancing and a DepthNormals pass) with DecoKitHarbour.Ocean's values: two wind-drifted layers of the old wave sheet (DK_Sea_Normal; tiles 42 and 11 m, slope 0.55, speed 1) flattening from 80 to 1600 m, a lit teal body (sRGB 0.05, 0.32, 0.42) with back-lit crests (0.1, 0.55, 0.5), Fresnel toward the reflection probe lifted toward the zenith (0.45) and capped (0.55), and the tight sun glitter (power 1200 x 40) that the bloom turns into sparkle. It replaces Suborned/Water for the district water and the horizon sea alike (one material, name `water`, so SeaFade and the far-shore fade are unchanged). Colours are given as DecoKitHarbour gave them (SetColor with the sRGB triple).

street.note: Glint, 026 chrome fix (briefs/027/latch/chrome). Chrome read flat pale grey because the default cube is haze (L 0.93) from the horizon up and only a short ramp to ground, so chrome outside the two probes mirrors nothing dark (cube mean luminance 0.56, 0% dark, 16% bright). A street canyon is dark at the horizon, mid-grey walls, bright only high up. Cube function (Latch, ReflectionCube.cs; no colour constants in C#): elevation e in degrees; below the horizon lerp groundHorizon to groundNadir over groundDepth; above it lerp wallBase to wall over baseHeight, then to the sky over bandHeight..bandHeight+bandSoft, where sky = lerp(horizon, zenith, skyMix * y^0.55) (y = sin e). The sun glow terms stay as they are. Palette values scale in HSV as every entry does.

streak.note: Glint 026 round 3: day chrome had tone and band (mean 0.35) but nothing above 0.8. A bright sky-window band toward the sun: displayed 0.97 (the cube is RGBA32, so it cannot exceed 1), 34 to 54 deg above the horizon, +-70 deg either side of the sun azimuth, 8 deg soft edges, replacing the sky colour there. About 4 percent of the sphere; chrome caps that face the sun and the sky get one bright streak, the rest keeps the dark band.

The Handover at night, LOOK ONLY: the sim, sight, schedules and every replay are untouched (Keel's rulebook has no light input; night changes nothing a rule reads).
